findings.reason: Attributes 'Assignment & approval workflows' to the $49/mo/client Agency plan, but source shows this feature listed only under the Premium tier, not confirmed for Agency plan.
Cost table pairs Statusbrew's Agency plan price with a feature ('Assignment & approval workflows') only sourced from the separate Premium tier.

findings.text: For an agency weighing collaboration features specifically, the choice comes down to how your client relationships are structured. Buffer's per-channel Team plan fits agencies that add and drop client channels regularly and want approval workflows bundled into one flat rate per channel with unlimited team members. Planable's per-workspace model fits agencies that want a hard Required approval gate isolated by client. Statusbrew's assignment and SLA features fit agencies whose bottleneck is routing incoming messages to the right person, not just approving outgoing posts. Whichever direction fits, verify the current terms on each vendor's own pricing page before you commit a client roster to it.
findings.reason: Making the Call restates the same tool-fit conclusions (Buffer for churn, Planable for required gate, Statusbrew for SLA routing) already given in the comparison section.

findings.text: If clients need strict separation and a hard "nothing publishes without sign-off" rule, Planable's Required approval tier or Statusbrew's assignment workflow map more directly onto that requirement than a flat team price does.
findings.reason: Statusbrew's page lists 'Assignment & approval workflows' as a feature but never states it enforces a mandatory nothing-publishes-without-sign-off rule like Planable's Required tier.
